prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help. To recommend the right lawyer I need a bit more info, but first here’s practical guidance so you can choose a good personal-injury attorney in Pleasanton (or I can pull local names for you if you want).

Quick questions
- When did the accident happen?
- Were you injured and have you seen a doctor?
- Who was at fault (your view)?
- Any police report? Any insurance contact yet?
- Do you suspect a government entity is involved (city bus, public road)?
- Do you want me to find local attorney names and contact info?

What kind of lawyer you need
- A personal injury car-accident attorney (one who handles auto collisions). Look for experience in California auto-injury cases, insurance negotiations, and trials.

Important deadlines (act quickly)
- In California the basic statute of limitations for personal injury is generally 2 years from the injury date. If a government agency is involved, much shorter deadlines usually apply (often 6 months to file a claim). Don’t delay contacting an attorney.

How to choose — key criteria
- Experience with car-accident cases and injuries similar to yours.
- Trial experience (many cases settle, but you want someone who will go to court if needed).
- Track record of settlements/verdicts and references.
- Contingency-fee arrangement (most take PI cases on contingency; typical contingency fees are in the 33%–40% range; get the exact percentage and expense policy in writing).
- Clear communication: who you’ll speak with, how often, and who handles work (attorney vs. paralegal).
- Local knowledge: familiarity with Alameda County courts, local hospitals, and adjusters.
- Professional reputation: State Bar status (no suspensions), client reviews, peer reviews.

What to ask at the free consultation
- Have you handled cases like mine? How many and what were the results?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day?
- What is your fee and how are costs handled?
- What is your estimated recovery range and timeline?
- Do you go to trial? What percentage of your cases go to trial vs settle?
- Can you provide client references or examples of past settlements/verdicts?
- How will you keep me informed?

Documents to bring to consultations
- Police report
- Photos of accident, vehicle damage, injuries, scene
- Medical records and bills, doctor notes
- Auto insurance policy and any correspondence with insurers
- Witness names/contact info
- Pay stubs if claiming lost wages
- Any repair estimates

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific dollar outcome
- Pressure to sign immediately
- No written fee agreement or unclear fee/cost terms
- Poor responsiveness during the first contact

How to verify credentials
- Check the State Bar of California website (calbar.ca.gov) for license status and discipline history.
- Look at client reviews (Google, Yelp), and lawyer directories (Avvo, Martindale).
- Ask for references.

Finding local lawyers
- Use the State Bar “Find a Lawyer” tool, the Alameda County Bar Association referral service, or consumer-review sites.
- If you want, I can compile a short list (3–5) of Pleasanton/Tri-Valley personal injury attorneys with links, contact info, and a quick summary of their experience.

Would you like me to:
A) Pull a short list of local Pleasanton/Tri-Valley car-accident attorneys for you to call? or
B) Help you draft questions and a checklist to use in consultations?

Tell me which and answer the quick questions above if you want personalized recommendations.
